messages:

Cc: Simone Hsu <simone.hsu@novatek.com>, procurement@novatek.com

Subject: Q4 expected traffic spike — temporary uplift & overage terms

Hi Karthish (hope I'm spelling that right),

We're running a pilot of the customer-facing search assistant that uses your hosted inference and expect a traffic spike the week of Nov 9 — roughly 3–4x our current sustained throughput for ~10 days. We can throttle/queue some requests on our side but the UX will degrade.

Two asks from procurement/engineering:
- Is there a short-term throughput uplift you can grant (rate-limit/burst) to cover the Nov 9–19 window?
- If we exceed our quota, what does the overage true-up process look like? Any one-time credits or capped overage pricing available for pilots?

Attached is our procurement intake form and a rough traffic projection. We're evaluating redlines on SLAs and want to keep costs predictable.

Can we jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to align?

Thanks,
Jordan Miles
Senior Product Manager, Novatek

Attachment: Novatek_Procurement_Form.pdf
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-30T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 expected traffic spike — temporary uplift & overage terms

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the projection. Short answer: yes, we can help cover a short-term uplift and we have a couple of approaches depending on your preference for predictability vs. flexibility.

High level options (we can formalize on a call):
1) Soft-cap uplift (recommended for trials): we temporarily raise your quota and configure a soft cap that allows bursts above committed throughput up to a defined ceiling. Overage charges still apply but at a reduced rate for the uplift window.
2) Pre-bought burst credits: you purchase a one-time block of burst credits at a discounted rate, applied automatically when your usage exceeds the baseline. No surprise invoices within the period.
3) Temporary rate-limit upgrade: for 10–14 days we move you to a higher rate class with a per-token overrun rate and optional true-up invoice at month-end.

For pilots we often combine option 1 with a modest promotional credit to offset unexpected overruns. If Novatek is open to converting to a reserved commit afterwards, we can extend a conversion credit that applies to the first invoice on the reserved plan.

Proposed next steps: 30-min call tomorrow (I cc'd Marissa from Sales Ops and Stephanie from Finance to surface procurement redlines). On the call we'll confirm: dates, uplift ceiling (tokens/sec), billing approach (credits vs overage rate), and doc signature path. I'll also send a draft soft-cap amendment with our suggested capped overage formula.

When are you free tomorrow morning PST?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-rate-plan-ailift.xlsx

Karthik, thanks — that list is helpful. Simone (cc) will own the procurement formalities; engineering wants the soft-cap approach if the billing is predictable. Proposed parameters from our side:
- Window: 2026-11-09 00:00 UTC through 2026-11-19 23:59 UTC
- Baseline: current purchased throughput (see attached)
- Uplift ceiling: +350% of baseline; preferred hard ceiling but willing to accept a soft cap with an explicit overage formula
- Target: limit customer-visible failures; prefer credits to surprise invoices for the pilot

We can do a call at 9:30 AM PST tomorrow.

Jordan

- If Novatek signs a 6-month reserved commit within 60 days, convert any unused credits into a one-time invoice credit equal to 20% of the uplift invoice (max $12k).
- Rate math: baseline overage rate = $0.0016 / token; uplift-rate = $0.0024 / token; promotional uplift-rate = $0.0012 / token (applies while credits remain).
